task.claim:
Let k be a field, R = k[x_1, ..., x_n], and F a subset of R generating the
ideal (F).

For each natural number i, let V_{F,i} be the smallest k-vector subspace of R
such that:
  - F intersected with R_{<=i} is contained in V_{F,i}; and
  - whenever f is in V_{F,i} and g is in R_{<= i - deg(f)}, the product fg is
    in V_{F,i}.

Define the last fall degree of F as
    d_F = min{ d : f is in V_{F, max(d, deg f)} for every f in (F) }.

For f in (F) define d_f = min{ d : f is in V_{F,d} }; note d_f >= deg(f)
always. Say f HAS A DEGREE FALL when d_f > deg(f), and say F has a degree
fall when some f in (F) does.

Assume d_F is finite and that F has a degree fall. Then

    d_F = max{ d_f : f in (F) and d_f > deg(f) }.

That is, the last fall degree is exactly the largest degree at which a degree
fall occurs.

Proof sketch (Caminata-Gorla, Theorem 2.8). For the inequality d_F >= sup:
if d_f > deg(f) then f is not in V_{F,d} for any d < d_f, so d_F > d_f - 1 by
the definition of last fall degree; finiteness of d_F turns the supremum into
a maximum. For the reverse: set mu equal to that maximum and fix f in (F). If
d_f > deg(f) then f is in V_{F,d_f} which is contained in V_{F,mu}, and
mu = max(mu, deg f) because mu >= d_f > deg(f). If d_f = deg(f) then f is in
V_{F,deg(f)} which is contained in V_{F,max(mu,deg f)}. Either way f lies in
V_{F,max(mu,deg f)} for every f in (F), so mu belongs to the set defining d_F
and hence d_F <= mu.
